name: Nelson Mandela
quote: Overcoming poverty is not a gesture of charity, it is an act of justice.

name: Margaret Thatcher
quote: There is no such thing as society: there are individual men and women, and there are families.
explain: You were aligned with Margaret Thatcher because your answers leaned toward personal responsibility, smaller government, and faith in free markets. You valued self-reliance over collective solutions.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
quote: You must be the change you wish to see in the world.
explain: You were aligned with Mahatma Gandhi because you valued nonviolent solutions, moral persuasion over state force, and progress through community ethics.

name: Thomas Jefferson
quote: I prefer dangerous freedom over peaceful slavery.
explain: You were aligned with Thomas Jefferson because your answers suggested that freedom and individual rights mattered more to you than strong state control.

name: Joseph Stalin

explain: You were aligned with Joseph Stalin because your answers showed support for heavy state control over the economy and society.

name: Charles de Gaulle
quote: Patriotism is when love of your own people comes first; nationalism, when hate for others comes first.

name: Adam Smith

explain: You were aligned with Adam Smith because your answers showed trust in free markets and competition to drive prosperity.

name: Karl Marx
quote: The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.
explain: You were aligned with Karl Marx because your answers emphasized reducing wealth gaps and prioritizing workers over private owners.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
quote: The test of our progress is not whether we add more to the abundance of those who have much; it is whether we provide enough for those who have little.
explain: You were aligned with FDR because you supported government safety nets, public spending, and programs to help the vulnerable.

name: Ronald Reagan
quote: The nine most terrifying words in the English language are: I'm from the government and I'm here to help.
explain: You were aligned with Ronald Reagan because your answers showed preference for lower taxes, smaller government, and a traditional outlook.

name: Winston Churchill
quote: Democracy is the worst form of government, except for all those other forms that have been tried.
explain: You were aligned with Winston Churchill because your answers valued order, duty, and stability in times of crisis.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
quote: Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.
explain: You were aligned with Martin Luther King Jr. because your answers emphasized equality, inclusivity, and progress.

name: Che Guevara
quote: The revolution is not an apple that falls when it is ripe. You have to make it fall.
explain: You were aligned with Che Guevara because your answers showed a willingness to challenge inequality through radical means.

name: Confucius
quote: The strength of a nation derives from the integrity of the home.
explain: You were aligned with Confucius because your answers highlighted respect for tradition, family, and social order.

name: John Locke
quote: Where there is no law, there is no freedom.
explain: You were aligned with John Locke because your answers valued individual rights, property, and government by consent.

name: Adolf Hitler
quote: He alone, who owns the youth, gains the future.
explain: You were aligned with Adolf Hitler because your answers leaned heavily toward centralized authority, extreme nationalism, and rigid traditionalism.

name: John F. Kennedy
quote: Ask not what your country can do for you – ask what you can do for your country.
explain: You were aligned with John F. Kennedy because your answers showed belief in civic duty, moderate government involvement, and global cooperation.

name: Angela Merkel
quote: We will manage this.
explain: You were aligned with Angela Merkel because your answers favored moderation, compromise, and steady leadership.

name: Malcolm X
quote: You can't separate peace from freedom because no one can be at peace unless he has his freedom.
explain: You were aligned with Malcolm X because your answers reflected a strong demand for justice, dignity, and self-reliance.

name: Barack Obama
quote: If we aren't willing to pay a price for our values, then we should ask ourselves whether we truly believe in them at all.
explain: You were aligned with Barack Obama because your answers supported progressive values, inclusivity, and fairness, while still valuing personal freedoms.

name: Milton Friedman
quote: Inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon.
explain: Friedman strongly favored free markets and limited government; socially tolerant and libertarian on many cultural issues (civil liberties, opposition to the draft, critiques of drug prohibition).

name: Ayn Rand
quote: The question isn't who is going to let me; it's who is going to stop me.
explain: Objectivist champion of laissez-faire capitalism and radical individual liberty; a polarizing figure—use `controversial: true` if needed.

name: Emma Goldman
quote: If I can't dance, I don't want to be part of your revolution.
explain: Anarchist and radical activist: strongly anti-state economically, fiercely pro-personal freedom socially, skeptical of state-driven foreign policy.

name: Mikhail Bakunin
quote: The urge to destroy is also a creative urge.
explain: Classical anarchist: extreme anti-statist economics with a strong libertarian social bent and general opposition to imperial intervention.

name: Friedrich A. Hayek
quote: The curious task of economics is to demonstrate to men how little they really know about what they imagine they can design.
explain: A foundational classical liberal: skeptical of central planning, pro-market, and wary of social engineering while valuing individual liberty.

name: Benito Mussolini
quote: Everything in the State, nothing outside the State, nothing against the State.
explain: Authoritarian, nationalistic leader favoring strong social control and an interventionist posture; economy was corporatist/state-directed rather than pure free market.

name: Juan Perón
quote: The people are what matter, not the leaders.
explain: Populist/corporatist blend: mixed economic policies with protectionism, socially conservative and nationalistic tendencies.

name: George Washington
quote: It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.
explain: Cautious internationalist in practice—warned against entangling alliances, favored pragmatic neutrality in foreign affairs.

name: Charles de Gaulle
quote: France cannot be France without greatness.
explain: Independent-minded leader skeptical of foreign dominance; favored a strong state and cautious foreign posture centered on national sovereignty.

name: Noam Chomsky
quote: If we don't believe in freedom of expression for people we despise, we don't believe in it at all.
explain: Critic of concentrated economic power and imperial foreign policy; combines left-leaning economic views with strong civil liberties.

name: Eugene V. Debs
quote: While there is a lower class, I am in it; while there is a criminal element, I am of it.
explain: Early American socialist and labor leader: pro-union, pro-redistribution, and democratic in social aims.

name: Bernie Sanders
quote: A political revolution is coming.
explain: Modern democratic-socialist politician advocating strong welfare, progressive taxation, and civil liberties; included as a contemporary anchor.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
quote: A moment comes, which comes but rarely in history, when we step out from the old to the new.
explain: Post-colonial leader favoring mixed-economy development and active non-aligned international engagement.

name: Kwame Nkrumah
quote: We face neither East nor West; we face forward.
explain: Pan-Africanist and development-oriented leader favoring state-led development and an engaged international stance for newly independent nations.

name: Mao Zedong
quote: Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun.
explain: Revolutionary communist leader who implemented radical state-led economic change and centralized political control; included as a controversial but important anchor.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
quote: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
explain: Existentialist philosopher and feminist: advocated for social liberation, gender equality, and challenged traditional hierarchies.

name: Edmund Burke
quote: Those who don't know history are destined to repeat it.
explain: Foundational conservative thinker: emphasized tradition, gradual change, and skepticism of radical reform while supporting organic social order.

name: Rosa Luxemburg
quote: Freedom is always the freedom of the one who thinks differently.
explain: Revolutionary socialist and theorist: combined strong anti-capitalist economics with democratic principles and internationalist outlook.

name: Lee Kuan Yew
quote: I am often accused of interfering in the private lives of citizens. Yet, if I did not, had I not done that, we wouldn't be here today.
explain: Pragmatic authoritarian modernizer: combined free-market capitalism with strong social control and emphasis on Asian values.

name: Simón Bolívar
quote: The art of victory is learned in defeat.
explain: Latin American liberator: fought for independence and republican government, balanced liberal ideals with pragmatic centralized authority.
